questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

The smallest dog barks the loud.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of "**the loud**" instead of the correct comparative form "**the loudest**".
 
• In English, superlative forms are used to describe the highest degree of a quality among three or more items.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**the loudest**", ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The smallest dog barks the loudest."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **2: "The smallest"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3: "dog barks"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 1.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

_____careful - that clock is very old.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Be'.

__
 
• The word "**Be**" is the imperative form of the verb "**to be**."
 
• The imperative form is used to give commands or instructions.
 
• **Options 1, 3**, and 4 are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Be careful - that clock is very old."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "Been"** is incorrect because "been" is the past participle of "be" and cannot be used in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "Being"** is incorrect because "being" is the present participle of "be" and cannot be used in this context.
 
• **Option 4: "I"** is incorrect because it does not fit grammatically in the sentence structure.

The family __was in mourning__ for a month.

Therefore, the correct answer is **No improvement**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The family was in mourning for a month."*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Anomaly
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Conformity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"anomaly"** means something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected. (विसंगति)

 
 
• **Example: **The scientist found an anomaly in the data that could not be explained by the current theory.
 
 
 
• **"Conformity" **refers to compliance with standards, rules, or laws; behavior in accordance with socially accepted conventions or standards. (अनुरूपता)
 
 
• **Example: **His conformity to the company's policies made him a model employee.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'anomaly' **is **'conformity'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Conformity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Abnormality **(असामान्यता): A feature or characteristic in an individual that is unusual or different from the typical.

 
 
• **Example:** The doctor noticed an abnormality in the patient's heartbeat.
 
 
 
• **Aberration **(विचलन): A departure from what is normal, usual, or expected, typically one that is unwelcome.
 
 
• **Example: **The sudden drop in temperature was an aberration from the usual weather patterns.
 
 
 
• **Deviation** (विचलन): The action of departing from an established course or accepted standard.
 
 
• **Example:** Any deviation from the plan could result in failure.

questions.question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

Sometimes you just need to stop **contemplating **over **the past** and make a decision.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Chew the cud**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Chew the cud"** means to think slowly and carefully about something over a period of time. (किसी चीज के बारे में धीरे-धीरे और ध्यानपूर्वक सोचना)

 
 
• **Example: **He sat in his chair chewing the cud, pondering over the events of the day.
 
 
 
• Sometimes you just need to stop contemplating over the past and make a decision. The idiom "Chew the cud" accurately describes the act of contemplating or thinking over something. (कभी-कभी आपको बस अतीत के बारे में सोचना बंद करने और एक निर्णय लेने की आवश्यकता होती है। "Chew the cud" वाक्यांश सोचने या किसी चीज पर विचार करने के कार्य का सही वर्णन करता है।)
 
 
• **Example: **Rather than continuously chewing the cud over past mistakes, it's better to take action and move forward.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Chew the cud**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Spill the beans **(राज़ खोल देना): To reveal secret information unintentionally.

 
 
• **Example:** He accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party planned for her.
 
 
 
• **Make no bones about **(स्पष्ट रूप से कहना): To speak directly and without hesitation.
 
 
• **Example: **She made no bones about her dissatisfaction with the service.
 
 
 
• **Tongue and cheek** (मज़ाक में): Something said in a humorous or ironic manner.
 
 
• **Example:** His tongue and cheek comments often lighten the mood in serious meetings.

questions.question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required if the sentence is correct as given.

Rusty's own house (back at Berlin do not even have) a name: it was just called number four.

options.text: back in Berlin didn't even have
back at Berlin doesn't even have

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'back at Berlin do not even have' is incorrect.
 
• The correct preposition to use with Berlin is **'in'**, not **'at'**.
 
• The plural subject **'house'** should be paired with **'doesn't'** instead of **'do not'**.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be **'back in Berlin didn't even have'**.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *Rusty's own house back in Berlin didn't even have a name: it was just called number four*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When referring to a location within a city, **'in'** is typically the correct preposition to use, as opposed to **'at'**.

 
 
• **Example:** *I live **in** New York, not **at** New York.*
 
 
 
• The phrase **'do not have'** should be adjusted to **'doesn't have'** when referring to a singular noun like 'house'.
 
 
• **Example:** *The car doesn't have any gas.*

questions.question:
**Choose the option which are antonyms (opposite of) the word used in the sentence given below:**

His altruistic efforts to raise money for charity were met with praise, but his selfish actions in hoarding resources for personal gain raised concerns about his true motivations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"altruistic"** means showing a selfless concern for the well-being of others. (निःस्वार्थ)

 
 
• **Example: **Her altruistic nature led her to volunteer at the local shelter every weekend.
 
 
 
• **"Selfish" **refers to someone who is primarily concerned with their own advantage and welfare, often at the expense of others. (स्वार्थी)
 
 
• **Example: **His selfish decision to not share the resources caused a lot of resentment among the team members.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'altruistic' **is **'selfish'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Hoarding/Gain **(भंडारण/लाभ): Hoarding refers to the accumulation of items in excess, typically for personal use. Gain refers to obtaining something, usually of value.

 
 
• **Example:** His hoarding of essential supplies during the crisis was condemned, even though he justified it as a gain for his family’s security.
 
 
 
• **Money/Charity **(पैसा/चैरिटी): Money refers to a medium of exchange, typically in the form of coins and banknotes. Charity refers to the voluntary giving of help, typically in the form of money, to those in need.
 
 
• **Example: **She decided to donate her money to charity to help those less fortunate.
 
 
 
• **Actions/Concerns** (कार्रवाई/चिंता): Actions refer to the fact or process of doing something. Concerns refer to a matter of interest or importance.
 
 
• **Example:** His actions were well-intended, but they raised concerns among the stakeholders.
